Course: ECE-S201 - Analog Electronics (Semester III, 5 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Develop comprehensive understanding of special-purpose semiconductor diodes; CO2 Analyze and design BJT-based amplifier circuits using small signal models and h-parameters; CO3 Impart knowledge on construction, operation, and characteristics of JFETs.

Subject: Analog Electronics (ECE-S201). Semester: III. Unit-I (Special Diodes): Review of PN Junction, Breakdown Mechanisms in Semiconductor Diodes, Zener Diode as regulator, Tunnel Diode, Varactor Diode, Photo Diode, Light Emitting Diode.

Subject: Analog Electronics (ECE-S201). Semester: III. Unit-II (Bipolar Junction Transistor & UJT): Transistor as Amplifier, small signal low frequency amplifier, CE amplifier graphical analysis, h-parameters model.

Subject: Analog Electronics (ECE-S201). Semester: III. Unit-III (Junction Field Effect Transistor (JFET)): Construction, principle of operation, Pinch-off Voltage, Volt-Ampere characteristics, FET parameters, Common Source & Common Drain Amplifiers.

Subject: Analog Electronics (ECE-S201). Semester: III. Unit-IV (MOSFET): Structure and physical operation of MOSFET, Enhancement and Depletion modes, I-V relationship in saturation and non-saturation regions.

Subject: Analog Electronics (ECE-S201). Semester: III. Unit-V (Multi Stage Amplifiers): Classification of amplifiers, RC coupled amplifier, transformer coupled amplifier, Direct coupled amplifier, Darlington pair amplifier.

Course: ECE-S202 - Digital Electronics & Logic Design (Semester III, 5 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Examine structure of number systems and perform conversion among different systems; CO2 Understand Digital Logic Families and Boolean algebra reduction via K-Maps; CO3 Design and analyze synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits using flip-flops.

Subject: Digital Electronics & Logic Design (ECE-S202). Semester: III. Unit-I (Logic Circuits & Boolean Algebra): Number systems, Gray code, BCD Code, Boolean algebra theorems, K-Map minimization, Logic families (RTL, DTL, TTL, ECL, CMOS).

Subject: Digital Electronics & Logic Design (ECE-S202). Semester: III. Unit-II (Combinational Circuits): Binary Adder/Subtractor, Parallel Adder, BCD Adder, Decoders, Multiplexers, Demultiplexers, Comparators, Seven-segment decoder.

Subject: Digital Electronics & Logic Design (ECE-S202). Semester: III. Unit-III (Sequential Circuits): Flip-Flops (RS, D, T, JK), Master-Slave Flip-Flops, Race around condition, Excitation tables, State diagrams.

Subject: Digital Electronics & Logic Design (ECE-S202). Semester: III. Unit-IV (Counters & Shift Registers): Asynchronous & Synchronous counters, Ripple counter, Up-Down counter, Ring counter, Shift registers.

Subject: Digital Electronics & Logic Design (ECE-S202). Semester: III. Unit-V (Multivibrators & Memories): Monostable, Bistable, Astable Multivibrators, Schmitt trigger, RAM, ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, PLAs, PALs, BiCMOS.

Course: ECE-S203 - Electromagnetic Theory (Semester III, 3 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Differentiate coordinate systems and use them for electromagnetic field problems; CO2 Describe static electric and magnetic fields, boundary conditions and potentials; CO3 Use integral and point form of Maxwell equations.
Subject: Electromagnetic Theory (ECE-S203). Semester: III. Unit-I (Electrostatics): Vector calculus, Coulomb's law, Gauss's Law, Electric Potential, Polarization, Poisson's and Laplace's equations.

Subject: Electromagnetic Theory (ECE-S203). Semester: III. Unit-II (Magnetostatics): Biot-Savart's law, Ampere's Circuital Law, Magnetic Flux density, Vector potentials, Magnetic boundary conditions, Inductance.

Subject: Electromagnetic Theory (ECE-S203). Semester: III. Unit-III (Maxwell's Equations & EM Waves): Faraday's Law, Displacement Current, Maxwell's Equations, Plane waves in lossless dielectrics, Poynting Vector.
Subject: Electromagnetic Theory (ECE-S203). Semester: III. Unit-IV (Transmission Lines): Transmission line parameters, Input impedance, SWR, Smith Chart applications.
Subject: Electromagnetic Theory (ECE-S203). Semester: III. Unit-V (Waveguides): Parallel Plate Waveguide, TE, TM, TEM modes, Rectangular Waveguide, Power transmission.

Course: ECE-S204 - Network Analysis and Synthesis (Semester III, 3 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand graph theory using different analysis methods; CO2 Apply network functions for electrical network analysis; CO3 Understand two port networks.
Subject: Network Analysis and Synthesis (ECE-S204). Semester: III. Unit-I (Graph Theory): Graph of network, Planar/Non-Planar graphs, Tree, Co-Tree, Cut set matrix, Tie set matrix, Nodal analysis.

Subject: Network Analysis and Synthesis (ECE-S204). Semester: III. Unit-II (Transient Circuit Analysis): Natural and forced response, Transient and steady state response for DC/AC inputs via Laplace methods.
Subject: Network Analysis and Synthesis (ECE-S204). Semester: III. Unit-III (Network Functions): Complex frequency, Transform impedances, Poles and zeros, Driving point and transfer functions.
Subject: Network Analysis and Synthesis (ECE-S204). Semester: III. Unit-IV (Two Port Networks): Z, Y, ABCD, h parameters, Interconnections of two port networks, T and Pi representations.

Subject: Network Analysis and Synthesis (ECE-S204). Semester: III. Unit-V (Network Synthesis & Filters): Positive real functions, Foster and Cauer synthesis of LC/RC/RL networks, Passive and Active Filters.

Course: ECE-S205 - Analog Integrated Circuits (Semester IV, 5 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand advantages of negative feedback and feedback amplifier topologies; CO2 Analyze Power Amplifiers (Class A, B, AB, C, Push-Pull); CO3 Design sinusoidal/non-sinusoidal oscillators and Op-Amp fundamentals.

Subject: Analog Integrated Circuits (ECE-S205). Semester: IV. Unit-I (Feedback Amplifiers & Topologies): Negative feedback advantages, Voltage series, current series, voltage shunt, current shunt, gain & phase margin.
Subject: Analog Integrated Circuits (ECE-S205). Semester: IV. Unit-II (Power Amplifiers): Class A, Class B, Class AB, Class C, Push-Pull configuration, Power BJTs, MOS Power Transistors, Heat sinks.

Subject: Analog Integrated Circuits (ECE-S205). Semester: IV. Unit-III (Oscillators & Op-Amp Fundamentals): Barkhausen criterion, RC phase shift, Wien bridge, Hartley, Colpitts oscillators, Current mirror, Active load.

Subject: Analog Integrated Circuits (ECE-S205). Semester: IV. Unit-IV (Op-Amp Applications & Active Filters): Inverting/non-inverting amplifiers, Integrator, Differentiator, Precision Rectifier, Schmitt trigger, Active Filters.
Subject: Analog Integrated Circuits (ECE-S205). Semester: IV. Unit-V (Data Converters & Wave Shaping): DAC/ADC, 555 Timer applications, Monostable/Astable operation, Ramp & Sawtooth generators.

Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-I (8085 & 8086 Microprocessor Architecture): 8085 Register structure, ALU, Bus organization. 8086 Internal organization, Bus interface unit, Execution unit.

Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-II (Assembly Language Programming): Addressing modes, Data transfer, Arithmetic/logical instructions, Jumps, Calls, Loops, Assembler Directives.

Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-III (CPU Module Design & 8087 Coprocessor): Pin configuration of 8086/8088, Demultiplexing, Minimum/Maximum mode operation, 8087 Numeric coprocessor.
Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-IV (Peripheral Interfacing): 8255 PPI, 8251 USART, 8259 PIC, 8237 DMA Controller, 8253/8254 Timer, ADC/DAC interfacing.
Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-V (Memory Interfacing): RAM & ROM Interfacing, Timing considerations, DRAM interfacing.

Subject: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers (ECE-S206). Semester: IV. Unit-VI (8051 Microcontroller Architecture): 8051 Architecture, Instruction set, Special Function Registers, Assembly language programming.

Course: ECE-S301 - Analog and Digital Communication (Semester V, 5 Credits). Branch: Electronics & Communication Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Apply statistical communication theory to analog/digital systems; CO2 Amplitude modulation (DSB-SC, SSB-SC, VSB) and noise calculation; CO3 Frequency modulation (FM/PM), PAM, PWM, PPM, PCM techniques.

Subject: Information Systems (DIT-S402). Semester: VIII. Unit 2 (OLAP vs OLTP & System Design): OLAP operations, Data mining for business intelligence, Decision trees, Decision tables.

Course: DIT-S551 - Cloud Computing (Semester VIII, 4 Credits). Branch: Information Technology. Course Outcomes: CO1 Describe principles of Parallel/Distributed Computing and Cloud evolution; CO2 Implement Virtualization technologies and Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA); CO3 Elucidate NIST Cloud Computing Architecture (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).
Subject: Cloud Computing (DIT-S551). Semester: VIII. Unit 1 (Cloud Paradigm & Architecture): NIST model, Grid vs Cloud computing, Public/Private/Hybrid clouds.
Subject: Cloud Computing (DIT-S551). Semester: VIII. Unit 2 (Virtualization & Service Models): Hypervisors, VM provisioning, IaaS (Amazon EC2), PaaS (Google App Engine), SaaS.
Subject: Cloud Computing (DIT-S551). Semester: VIII. Unit 3 (Cloud Security & Storage): SLA management, Cloud security governance, Data privacy, Identity & Access Management (IAM).

Course: MEES201 - Basic Fluid Mechanics (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 State Newton's law of viscosity and explain mechanics of fluids at rest and motion; CO2 Derive Euler's equation of motion and deduce Bernoulli's equation; CO3 Compute force of buoyancy on submerged bodies and analyze pipe energy losses.
Subject: Basic Fluid Mechanics (MEES201). Semester: III. Unit-I (Fluid Statics): Viscosity, Surface tension, Manometers, Buoyancy, Center of buoyancy, Stability of floating bodies.

Subject: Basic Fluid Mechanics (MEES201). Semester: III. Unit-II (Fluid Kinematics & Dynamics): Streamlines, Continuity equation, Euler's equation, Bernoulli's equation, Venturimeter, Orifice meter, Pitot tube.

Subject: Basic Fluid Mechanics (MEES201). Semester: III. Unit-III (Boundary Layer & Pipe Flow): Laminar and turbulent boundary layers, Drag and Lift, Darcy-Weisbach equation, Moody's chart, Hydraulic gradient line.

Course: MEES202 - Kinematics of Machine (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Identify link, pair, chain, joints and inversions of mechanisms; CO2 Construct velocity and acceleration diagrams for different mechanisms; CO3 Understand Cam profile generation and their applications.

Subject: Kinematics of Machine (MEES202). Semester: III. Unit-I (Kinematic Chains & Mechanisms): Links, Kinematic pairs, Degrees of freedom, Inversions of four-bar chain, Slider-crank mechanism, Velocity & Acceleration analysis.
Subject: Kinematics of Machine (MEES202). Semester: III. Unit-II (Cam Synthesis & Balancing): Cam profile synthesis, Flywheel, Inertia forces, Balancing of rotating & reciprocating masses.

Course: MEES203 - Manufacturing Science (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand fundamentals and analysis of Forging and Rolling processes; CO2 Knowledge of wire drawing, extrusion, sheet metal working, HERF processes; CO3 Understand principles of gas, arc, TIG, MIG, resistance welding and metallurgy.
Subject: Manufacturing Science (MEES203). Semester: III. Unit-I (Metal Forming & Sheet Metal): Forging, Rolling, Wire drawing, Extrusion, Press work, Blanking, Piercing, Deep drawing, HERF.
Subject: Manufacturing Science (MEES203). Semester: III. Unit-II (Welding Processes): Gas welding, Arc welding, TIG, MIG, Resistance welding, Soldering, Brazing, HAZ defects.

Subject: Manufacturing Science (MEES203). Semester: III. Unit-III (Casting (Foundry)): Pattern allowances, Molding sand properties, Gating system, Risers, Cupola furnace, Die casting, Centrifugal casting.

Subject: Manufacturing Science (MEES203). Semester: III. Unit-IV (Metal Cutting & Grinding): Merchant's force circle, Tool geometry ASA system, Chip formation, Tool wear & life, Grinding wheel specification.

Course: MEES205 - Basic Solid Mechanics (Semester IV, 3 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Analyze behavior of solid bodies subjected to various loading types; CO2 Apply structural element analysis to simple mechanical structures; CO3 Compute slope, deflection, bending stresses and shear stresses in beams.
Subject: Basic Solid Mechanics (MEES205). Semester: IV. Unit-I (Stress, Strain & Compound Stresses): Elastic constants, Plane stress, Principal stress/strain, Mohr's circle, Axially loaded members.
Subject: Basic Solid Mechanics (MEES205). Semester: IV. Unit-II (SFD, BMD & Beam Bending): Shear Force Diagram (SFD), Bending Moment Diagram (BMD), Flexural formula, Torsion of circular shafts.

Subject: Basic Solid Mechanics (MEES205). Semester: IV. Unit-III (Deflection, Columns & Pressure Vessels): Deflection of beams, Energy methods, Euler's column buckling, Thin & thick cylinders, Springs.

Course: MEES206 - Material Science & Engineering (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Know crystalline structure, crystal imperfections and defects; CO2 Understand phase diagrams and phase transformations in materials; CO3 Understand heat treatment processes (annealing, normalizing, hardening, tempering).

Subject: Material Science & Engineering (MEES206). Semester: IV. Unit-I (Crystal Structure & Imperfections): Crystalline solids, Crystal defects, Point/line/surface defects, Tensile & plastic properties, Creep, Fracture.

Subject: Material Science & Engineering (MEES206). Semester: IV. Unit-II (Phase Diagrams & Heat Treatment): Iron-Carbon equilibrium diagram, TTT diagram, Annealing, Normalizing, Quenching, Tempering, Case hardening.

Subject: Material Science & Engineering (MEES206). Semester: IV. Unit-III (Engineering Materials & Ceramics): Plain carbon steel, Alloy steels, Aluminium/Copper/Nickel alloys, Ceramics, Polymers, Composite materials, Smart materials.

Course: MEES207 - Dynamics of Machines (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Identify problems associated with unbalance in rotating & reciprocating machines; CO2 Realize requirements of frictional devices (clutches, brakes, dynamometers); CO3 Identify type of governors suited for speed control applications.

Subject: Dynamics of Machines (MEES207). Semester: IV. Unit-I (Force Analysis & Turning Moment): D'Alembert's principle, Dynamic force analysis of slider crank, Turning moment diagram, Flywheel design.

Subject: Dynamics of Machines (MEES207). Semester: IV. Unit-II (Governors & Gyroscopic Motion): Centrifugal governors (Watt, Porter, Proell, Hartnell), Gyroscopic couple, Stability of aircrafts & ships.

Subject: Dynamics of Machines (MEES207). Semester: IV. Unit-III (Balancing & Friction Devices): Static & Dynamic balancing, Reciprocating engine balancing, Clutches (single/multi-plate, cone), Brakes, Dynamometers.

Course: MEES301 - Heat Transfer & Mass Transfer (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand basic heat transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, radiation); CO2 Solve 1D steady & transient conduction in solids (rectangular, cylindrical, spherical); CO3 Calculate heat transfer from extended surfaces (fins) and natural/forced convection.
Subject: Heat Transfer & Mass Transfer (MEES301). Semester: V. Unit-I (Conduction Heat Transfer): 1D heat conduction equation, Critical thickness of insulation, Composite walls & cylinders.

Subject: Heat Transfer & Mass Transfer (MEES301). Semester: V. Unit-II (Fins & Natural Convection): Heat transfer from fins, Thermal boundary layer, Grashof & Rayleigh numbers, Combined free/forced convection.

Subject: Heat Transfer & Mass Transfer (MEES301). Semester: V. Unit-III (Forced Convection, Boiling & Heat Exchangers): Empirical relations for pipe flow, Pool boiling curve, LMTD and NTU heat exchanger design.

Subject: Heat Transfer & Mass Transfer (MEES301). Semester: V. Unit-IV (Thermal Radiation & Mass Transfer): Planck's law, Wein's law, Radiation shields, Fick's law of diffusion, Mass transfer rate equations.

Course: MEES302 - Fluid Machinery System (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Analyze principles of jet propulsion and impact forces; CO2 Evaluate performance and design of impulse (Pelton) and reaction (Francis, Kaplan) turbines; CO3 Apply dimensional analysis and model similitude to fluid machinery.
Subject: Fluid Machinery System (MEES302). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Impact of Free Jets): Impulse-Momentum principle, Jet impingement on flat/curved vanes, Jet propulsion of ships.
Subject: Fluid Machinery System (MEES302). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Impulse & Reaction Turbines): Pelton wheel construction & governing, Francis turbine, Kaplan turbine, Draft tube, Cavitation.

Subject: Fluid Machinery System (MEES302). Semester: V. Unit 3 (Pumps & Hydraulic Systems): Centrifugal pump manometric head & NPSH, Reciprocating pump indicator diagram, Air vessels, Hydraulic Ram & Press.

Course: MEES305 - Machine Design (Semester V, 3 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Select engineering materials and understand design considerations & standards; CO2 Design machine elements under static and dynamic (fatigue) loading; CO3 Analyze and design riveted, welded, cotter, shaft, key, coupling joints.
Subject: Machine Design (MEES305). Semester: V. Unit-I (Design Standards & Material Selection): ASTM testing methods, Steel designations, Creep and fatigue material selection.
Subject: Machine Design (MEES305). Semester: V. Unit-II (Static & Dynamic Design): Failure theories, Factor of safety, Stress concentration, Endurance limit, Soderberg & Goodman diagrams.
Subject: Machine Design (MEES305). Semester: V. Unit-III (Joints, Shafts & Couplings): Riveted/welded/cotter joints, Shaft strength & rigidity design, Rigid & flexible couplings.
Subject: Machine Design (MEES305). Semester: V. Unit-IV (Springs, Power Screws & Gears): Helical & leaf springs, Screw jack threads, Spur/Helical/Bevel/Worm gear module & speed diagrams.

Course: MEES306 - Computer Aided Design (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand applications of computers in mechanical design; CO2 Develop mathematical representations of curves (Spline, Bezier, B-Spline); CO3 Develop mathematical representations of solids (CSG, B-Rep).
Subject: Computer Aided Design (MEES306). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Computer Graphics & Curve Representation): Display file structure, Spline curves, Bezier curves, B-Splines, 2D/3D transformations.
Subject: Computer Aided Design (MEES306). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Solid Modeling & FEM Basics): Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG), Boundary Representation (B-Rep), 1D/2D spring & beam FEM analysis.

Course: MEES307 - Refrigeration and Air Conditioning (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand principles and applications of refrigeration cycles (Carnot, Bell-Coleman); CO2 Analyze performance of Vapour Compression Refrigeration Systems (VCRS); CO3 Analyze air conditioning processes using psychrometric charts.

Subject: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning (MEES307). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Air Refrigeration & VCRS): Bell-Coleman cycle, Aircraft refrigeration, Refrigerants classification, VCRS subcooling & superheating.

Subject: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning (MEES307). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Vapour Absorption & Psychrometrics): LiBr-water & Ammonia-water absorption systems, Psychrometric terms, Wet bulb temperature, Comfort charts.

Subject: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning (MEES307). Semester: VI. Unit 3 (Air Conditioning Equipment & Load Design): Duct design, Expansion valves, Cooling towers, Cooling & heating load calculations.

Course: MEES401 - Computer Aided Manufacturing (Semester VII, 4 Credits). Branch: Mechanical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Educate students on NC, CNC, DNC automation systems; CO2 Gain working knowledge of CNC machines, machine tools, drives, ball screws; CO3 Understand industrial robotics, ATC, APC, FMS shop floor layout.

Subject: Computer Aided Manufacturing (MEES401). Semester: VII. Unit 1 (NC/CNC Machine Construction): NC vs CNC vs DNC, Recirculating ball screws, Feedback transducers, Automatic Tool Changer (ATC), Tooling.
Subject: Computer Aided Manufacturing (MEES401). Semester: VII. Unit 2 (CNC Part Programming & FMS): ISO G & M codes, Canned cycles, Subroutines, Tool radius compensation, FMS, CIM, Robotics.

Course: MSES201 - Crystal Structure of Materials (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Classify Materials Based on Structure and Properties; CO2 Explain Types of Chemical Bonding in Solids; CO3 Understand Crystal Geometry and Lattice Concepts.

Subject: Crystal Structure of Materials (MSES201). Semester: III. Unit 1 (Crystal Geometry & Bonding): Classification of materials, Single/polycrystalline, Unit cells, Bravais lattices, Miller indices, Reciprocal lattices, Ionic/covalent/metallic bonding.

Subject: Crystal Structure of Materials (MSES201). Semester: III. Unit 2 (Imperfections & XRD): Point/line/surface defects, Coherent/incoherent interfaces, Frenkel & Schottky defects, Bragg's Law, Powder method XRD.

Course: MSES202 - Nature and Properties of Materials (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Apply Quantum Mechanical Principles to Material Behavior; CO2 Analyze Electrical and Magnetic Properties of Materials; CO3 Evaluate Thermal and Optical Properties of Solids.

Subject: Nature and Properties of Materials (MSES202). Semester: III. Unit 1 (Electronic & Magnetic Properties): Free electron theory, Fermi energy, Band theory, Semiconductors, Hall effect, Dielectric, Piezoelectric, Ferroelectric, Para/Dia/Ferro/Ferrimagnetism.

Subject: Nature and Properties of Materials (MSES202). Semester: III. Unit 2 (Thermal & Optical Properties): Specific heat, Thermal conductivity, Expansion, Thermoelectricity, Refractive index, Absorption, Lasers.

Subject: Nature and Properties of Materials (MSES202). Semester: III. Unit 3 (Mechanical Properties): Stress-strain response, Yield strength, Tensile strength, Modulus of elasticity, Creep, Fatigue, Fracture.

Course: MSES203 - Phase Equilibria in Materials (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Apply Phase Rule and Lever Rule to Binary Systems; CO2 Analyze Solidification Mechanisms and Microstructural Evolution; CO3 Evaluate Complex Phase Reactions and Intermediate Phases.

Subject: Phase Equilibria in Materials (MSES203). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Binary Phase Diagrams & Solidification): Phase rule, Lever rule, Isomorphous systems, Eutectic, Peritectic, Monotectic, Syntectic systems, Hume-Rothery rules, Spinodal decomposition.

Subject: Phase Equilibria in Materials (MSES203). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Ternary Diagrams & Engineering Alloys): Ternary phase diagrams, Gibbs triangle, Isothermal tie-lines, Stainless steels, High speed steels, Hadfield steels, Superalloys.

Course: MSES204 - Metallurgical Thermodynamics (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand and Apply Laws of Thermodynamics to Metallurgical Systems; CO2 Analyze Thermodynamic Functions and Maxwell Relations; CO3 Evaluate Solution Behavior, Raoult's and Henry's Laws, and Phase Equilibria.

Subject: Metallurgical Thermodynamics (MSES204). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Thermodynamic Functions & Solutions): First, Second & Third laws, Enthalpy, Gibbs free energy, Clausius-Clapeyron equation, Raoult's & Henry's laws, Activity coefficients, Gibbs-Duhem equation.

Subject: Metallurgical Thermodynamics (MSES204). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Ellingham Diagrams & Electrochemistry): Equilibrium constant, Ellingham diagrams, Phase stability, Nernst equation, Potential-pH (Pourbaix) diagrams.

subject_name: Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining
concept_content: Course: MSES205 - Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Sources and Preparation of Raw Materials; CO2 Analyze Mineral Beneficiation and Agglomeration Techniques (Sintering, Pelletizing); CO3 Perform Material and Energy Balances in Metallurgical Processes.

subject_name: Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining
concept_content: Subject: Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining (MSES205). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Mineral Beneficiation & Agglomeration): Comminution, Tabling, Jigging, Flotation, Gravity separation, Sintering, Pelletizing, Briquetting.

subject_name: Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining
concept_content: Subject: Principles of Metal Extraction and Refining (MSES205). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Extractive & Pyro-Metallurgy): Material & Energy balances, Hydrometallurgy, Electrometallurgy, Extraction of Al, Cu, Zn, Ti, Roasting, Smelting, Refining.

Course: MSES301 - Phase Transformation in Metals (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Thermodynamics and Nucleation Kinetics of Phase Transformations; CO2 Analyze Growth Mechanisms During Phase Transformations; CO3 Apply Kinetic Models (Johnson-Mehl, Avrami) to Phase Transformation Analysis.

Subject: Phase Transformation in Metals (MSES301). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Nucleation & Growth Kinetics): Homogeneous & Heterogeneous nucleation, Diffusion-controlled growth, Widmanstatten growth, Eutectoid growth, Avrami model.

Subject: Phase Transformation in Metals (MSES301). Semester: V. Unit 2 (TTT Diagrams & Recrystallization): Isothermal & Continuous cooling transformation (TTT & CCT) diagrams, Grain growth kinetics, Metallic glasses.

Course: MSES302 - Mechanical Behaviour of Materials (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Stress, Strain, and Elastic Behavior using Tensors and Mohr's Circle; CO2 Analyze Plastic Deformation and Dislocation Mechanics (Slip, Twinning); CO3 Evaluate Strengthening Mechanisms (Work Hardening, Grain Boundary, Precipitation).

Subject: Mechanical Behaviour of Materials (MSES302). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Stress Tensors & Dislocation Theory): Stress/Strain tensors, Elasticity, Yield criteria, Slip & Twinning, Edge/Screw dislocations, Dislocation interactions.

Subject: Mechanical Behaviour of Materials (MSES302). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Strengthening & Failure Mechanics): Strain hardening, Grain boundary strengthening, Griffith theory, Linear elastic fracture mechanics, Fatigue, Creep rupture.

Course: MSES304 - Iron Making (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Historical Development and Fundamentals of Iron Making; CO2 Analyze Chemical Reactions and Thermodynamics in Blast Furnace; CO3 Evaluate Raw Materials and Burden Preparation (Sintering, Pelletization, Coke).
Subject: Iron Making (MSES304). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Blast Furnace Reactions & Thermodynamics): BF shape, zones, Direct & indirect reduction, Sintering, Pelletization, Burden distribution.

Subject: Iron Making (MSES304). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Slag Chemistry & Alternative Routes): Slag basicity, Sulphide & phosphate capacity, Sponge iron (DRI), Smelting reduction, BF material & heat balances.

Course: MSES305 - Transport Phenomenon and Rate Processes (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Fundamental Principles of Momentum Transfer in Metallurgical Flow; CO2 Analyze Heat Transfer Mechanisms (Conduction, Convection, Radiation); CO3 Apply Mass Transfer Concepts, Diffusion Laws, and Fick's Laws.

Subject: Transport Phenomenon and Rate Processes (MSES305). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Momentum, Heat & Mass Transport): Viscosity, Shell balances, Bernoulli equation, Fourier's law, Convection coefficients, Radiation, Fick's laws.

Subject: Transport Phenomenon and Rate Processes (MSES305). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Kinetics & Dimensional Analysis): Buckingham Pi theorem, Arrhenius relation, Heterogeneous reaction kinetics, Oxidation & Electrochemical kinetics.

Course: MSE-S307 - Materials Characterization (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Fundamentals and Applications of Optical Microscopy; CO2 Gain Proficiency in Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM); CO3 Apply X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) for Crystallographic and Residual Stress Analysis.

Subject: Materials Characterization (MSE-S307). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Optical & Scanning Electron Microscopy): Phase contrast, Polarised light, SEM instrumentation, Sample preparation, Secondary & Backscattered electron imaging.
Subject: Materials Characterization (MSE-S307). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (XRD & Transmission Electron Microscopy): Bragg's law, Crystallite size, Peak broadening, TEM diffraction & image formation.

Subject: Materials Characterization (MSE-S307). Semester: VI. Unit 3 (Spectroscopy & Thermal Analysis): UV-Vis, IR, Raman spectroscopy, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA).

Course: MSES308 - Heat Treatment of Metals (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Heat Treatment Operations for Steels and Cast Irons; CO2 Understand Phase Transformations, Hardenability, TTT and CCT Diagrams; CO3 Analyze Quench Hardening, Tempering, Martensitic Transformation, and Retained Austenite.

Subject: Heat Treatment of Metals (MSES308). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Fe-C Diagram & Transformation Curves): Iron-Carbon phase diagram, Hardenability, TTT diagrams, CCT diagrams, Martensitic transformation kinetics.

Subject: Heat Treatment of Metals (MSES308). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Hardening, Tempering & Surface Treatments): Quench hardening, Tempering of martensite, Carburizing, Nitriding, Carbonitriding, Superalloys heat treatment.

Course: MSE-S309 - Steel Making (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Materials Science and Metallurgical Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand Modern Steelmaking Routes (BF-BOF, DRI-EAF, SR) and Thermodynamics; CO2 Analyze Primary Steelmaking Processes (LD Converter, EAF, Induction Furnace); CO3 Comprehend Secondary Steelmaking Techniques (Ladle Deoxidation, Vacuum Degassing, RH Degasser).
Subject: Steel Making (MSE-S309). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Primary Steelmaking Routes): BF-BOF, DRI-EAF, LD converter process, Catch carbon technique, Slag evolution, Electric Arc Furnace.

Subject: Steel Making (MSE-S309). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Secondary Steelmaking & Casting): Deoxidation kinetics, Vacuum degassing, Ladle desulphurization, Calcium treatment, Continuous casting, NDT testing.

Course: CSES201 - Data Structure (Semester III, 5 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Learn basic types for data structure, implementation and application; CO2 Know the strength and weakness of different data structures; CO3 Use appropriate data structure in context of solution of given problem.
Subject: Data Structure (CSES201). Semester: III. Unit 1 (Arrays, Stacks & Queues): Recursion, Sequential representation of Stacks and Queues, Circular Queues.
Subject: Data Structure (CSES201). Semester: III. Unit 2 (Linked Lists & Sorting): Dynamic Storage allocation, Doubly linked list, Insertion/Bubble/Quick/Merge/Heap/Shell sort.
Subject: Data Structure (CSES201). Semester: III. Unit 3 (Trees, Graphs & Hashing): Binary Search Trees (BST), Preorder/Inorder/Postorder traversals, B-Trees, B+ Trees, Graphs BFS & DFS, Hash tables.

Course: CSES202 - Digital Electronics and Logic Design (Semester III, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Convert different type of codes and number systems used in digital communication; CO2 Employ code converting circuits and compare logic families (RTL, DTL, TTL, ECL, CMOS); CO3 Analyze digital electronic circuits using K-Maps and Quine McCluskey method.

Subject: Digital Electronics and Logic Design (CSES202). Semester: III. Unit 1 (Boolean Algebra & Logic Families): Number systems, K-Maps, Quine McCluskey method, Prime implicants, TTL, ECL, CMOS logic families.

Subject: Digital Electronics and Logic Design (CSES202). Semester: III. Unit 2 (Combinational & Sequential Logic): Adders, Subtractors, Encoders, Decoders, MUX, DEMUX, ROM, PAL, PLA, Flip-Flops (RS, JK, D, T), State diagrams, VHDL.

Course: CSES204 - Object Oriented Programming (Using Java) (Semester IV, 5 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand basic concepts of Procedure-Oriented vs Object-Oriented Programming; CO2 Achieve knowledge of developing simple Java programs; CO3 Develop computer programs to solve real-world problems.
Subject: Object Oriented Programming (Using Java) (CSES204). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Java OOP Basics): Objects, Classes, Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Packages, Interfaces.
Subject: Object Oriented Programming (Using Java) (CSES204). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Java Applets & GUI): Applets, Swings, Multithreading, File I/O, Exception handling, Event-handling.

Course: CSES205 - Computer Organization (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Explain organizational and architectural issues of a digital computer; CO2 Describe data transfer techniques and I/O interfaces; CO3 Analyze performance of memories and ALU arithmetic implementation.
Subject: Computer Organization (CSES205). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Processor Arithmetic & ALU): Integer & floating point representation, Booth's algorithm, Half/Full adders, ALU design.
Subject: Computer Organization (CSES205). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Memory & Control Unit): RAM, ROM, DRAM vs SRAM, Cache mapping functions, Pipelined architectures, Hardwired vs Microprogrammed control.

Course: CSES206 - Operating System (Semester IV, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand services provided by Operating System at different levels; CO2 Learn real life applications of Operating System in every field; CO3 Understand CPU scheduling algorithms and process synchronization to avoid deadlocks.
Subject: Operating System (CSES206). Semester: IV. Unit 1 (Process Management & Deadlocks): Process synchronization, Semaphores, Monitors, CPU Scheduling (SJF, FCFS, Round Robin), Deadlock avoidance.
Subject: Operating System (CSES206). Semester: IV. Unit 2 (Memory & File Systems): Paging, Segmentation, Page replacement algorithms, Virtual memory, File protection, Access rights.

Course: CSES301 - Database Management Systems (Semester V, 5 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Describe fundamental elements of relational database management systems; CO2 Explain relational data model, ER-model, relational algebra and SQL; CO3 Design ER-models to represent database application scenarios.
Subject: Database Management Systems (CSES301). Semester: V. Unit 1 (ER Modeling & Relational Algebra): DBMS Architecture, Entity-Relationship Model, Relational Algebra, Tuple & Domain Calculus.
Subject: Database Management Systems (CSES301). Semester: V. Unit 2 (SQL & Normalization): SQL DDL, DML, Subqueries, Functional Dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, Lossless join decomposition.
Subject: Database Management Systems (CSES301). Semester: V. Unit 3 (Transactions & Concurrency): ACID properties, Serializability, Concurrency Control, Lock-based protocols, Recovery algorithms.

Course: CSES302 - Design and Analysis of Algorithms (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Ability to decide appropriate data type and data structure for a given problem; CO2 Ability to select best algorithm by considering data size and operation complexity; CO3 Ability to compare algorithms with respect to time and space complexity.
Subject: Design and Analysis of Algorithms (CSES302). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Asymptotic Analysis & Sorting): Big-O, Theta, Omega notations, Recurrence relations, Stable matching, Order statistics.

Subject: Design and Analysis of Algorithms (CSES302). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Graph & Paradigm Design): BFS, DFS, Dijkstra's shortest path, Kruskal's & Prim's MST, Divide & Conquer (Mergesort, Quicksort), Greedy method (Knapsack).

Subject: Design and Analysis of Algorithms (CSES302). Semester: V. Unit 3 (Dynamic Programming & NP-Completeness): 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence, Matrix chain multiplication, Network Flow, NP-Complete problems, Polynomial time approximation.

Course: CSES303 - Microprocessor (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Assess and solve basic binary math operations using microprocessor 8085/8086; CO2 Apply addressing modes and data transfer instructions in assembly programming; CO3 Compare 8085 Microprocessor and Microcontroller standards.
Subject: Microprocessor (CSES303). Semester: V. Unit 1 (8085 & 8086 Architecture): 8085 Architecture, Memory interfacing, I/O interfacing, Assembly language programming, 8085 instruction set.

Subject: Microprocessor (CSES303). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Interfacing & Peripheral Devices): Counters & Delays, Stack & Subroutines, BCD Arithmetic, Interrupts, D/A & A/D converters, 8255 PPI, 8259 PIC.

Course: CSES304 - Theory of Computation (Semester V, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Design Finite Automata machines for given computational problems; CO2 Analyze a given Finite Automata machine and find out its Language; CO3 Design Pushdown Automata (PDA) for given Context-Free Languages.

Subject: Theory of Computation (CSES304). Semester: V. Unit 1 (Finite Automata & Regular Languages): DFA, NFA, Regular grammars, Regular expressions, Equivalence of machines, Minimization of automata.
Subject: Theory of Computation (CSES304). Semester: V. Unit 2 (Context-Free Languages & PDA): CFG simplification, Chomsky Normal Form (CNF), Greibach Normal Form (GNF), Pushdown Automata.

Subject: Theory of Computation (CSES304). Semester: V. Unit 3 (Turing Machines & Undecidability): Turing machines, Computable functions, Church's thesis, Decidability, Undecidability, Halting problem.

Course: CSES305 - Compiler Design (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering. Course Outcomes: CO1 Understand fundamentals of compiler and relationships among different phases; CO2 Understand finite state machines, recursive descent parsing, production rules; CO3 Analyze and implement front-end, back-end, and middle-end optimizations.

Subject: Compiler Design (CSES305). Semester: VI. Unit 1 (Lexical & Syntax Analysis): Phases of compiler, Tokens, Lexemes, Regular definitions, LEX, CFGs, Top-down & Bottom-up parsing, LL(1), LR, SLR, LALR, YACC.

Subject: Compiler Design (CSES305). Semester: VI. Unit 2 (Intermediate Code & Optimization): Syntax Directed Definitions, Three-address code, Quadruples, Triples, Code optimization DAGs, Peephole optimization, Register allocation.

Course: CSES306 - Computer Networks (Semester VI, 4 Credits). Branch: Computer Science and Engineering.
